formal_contract.rule: For every main latency case, repeat 0 is the first TMA use of a newly allocated TensorMap and repeat 1 immediately reuses the same address and contents. Explicitly labelled payload-residency and prefetch controls may prime descriptor state outside the timed region and must record that exception.
formal_contract.cold_definition: Before repeat 0, no TMA command and no prefetch.tensormap has consumed the descriptor. Ordinary loads may make its bytes L2-resident where the suite explicitly records that state.
formal_contract.hot_definition: Repeat 1 uses the exact same TensorMap address and fingerprint after repeat 0 completes, with no explicit prefetch inserted between the two commands.
formal_contract.identity_evidence: Every Tensor row records descriptor address, fingerprint, prior_tma_use, pair_role and tma_prefetch_before_issue. Main latency validation requires 0 then 1; payload-residency v5 requires 1 then 2 after its recorded untimed primer. Identity remains equal within a pair and different between cases.
formal_contract.old_data_policy: FreshTensorMapV1 is retracted because it measured two independent cold descriptors instead of a natural cold-then-hot pair. It is removed after every ColdThenHotV1 replacement validates.
